title: WPSB/136/2014 of Dr. Mukesh Kumar Pandey Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (SB) No. 136 of 2014
Dr. Mukesh Kumar Pandey. ............ Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & another. ............. Respondents
&
Writ Petition (SB) No. 89 of 2015
Dr. Sandeep Kumar Dixit. ............ Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & another. ............. Respondents
Mr. Manoj Tiwari, Senior Advocate, assisted by Ms. Swati Verma, Advocate for the
petitioners.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand / respondents.
JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Dated: 16th December, 2015
K.M. JOSEPH, C.J. (Oral)
 As the writ petitions, two in number, raise common issues, they are
being disposed of by this common judgment.
2. The controversy in issue relates to promotion to the post of Joint
Director. The petitioners, in essence, rely on the principle that
uncommunicated adverse remarks must be eschewed for being considered
for promotion.
3. Pleadings have been exchanged. We have heard the learned Senior
Counsel appearing for the petitioners and the learned Standing Counsel
for the State.
4. The learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners would submit that it
is a case, where the petitioners have been given entries, which are

2
adverse. For instance, in Writ Petition (SB) No. 136 of 2014, for the
years 2007-2008 and 2008-2009, petitioner has been given entry
'outstanding'; whereas, in the next two years, petitioner has been given
'good' and 'achcha'. Resultantly, the position is as stated in paragraph 18
of the counter affidavit filed on behalf of respondent No. 1:

5. There is no dispute that the entries for the years, in which he got
'good' and 'achcha' have not been communicated to the petitioner.
Therefore, the contention of the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner
is that they are to be ignored and the claim of the petitioner must be
considered for promotion in terms of the law laid down in the case of Dev
Dutt vs. Union of India & others, reported in (2008) 8 SCC 725.
6. According to the Government, the entry 'good' cannot be treated as
adverse as such. It is not disputed, however, that the entries were not
communicated. The prayers made in Writ Petition (SB) No. 136 of 2014
are as follows:
"(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus declaring denial of promotion to Joint
Director Grade to the petitioner on the basis of
uncommunicated A.C.R. entries, as arbitrary and
violative of law laid down by the Apex Court in the
case of Dev Dutt. Vs. Union of India.
(ii) to declare the downgraded AC.R. ratings recorded
against the petitioner for reporting year 2009-10 and
2010-11 without recording any reason and without
informing petitioner about the change, as arbitrary and
illegal.
(iii) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus commanding the respondent no.1 to hold

3
review Departmental Promotion Committee and to
consider the petitioner's claim for promotion to Joint
Director's Grade after ignoring the uncommunicated
A.C.R. entries for the reporting year 2009-10 and
2010-11.
(iv) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus commanding the respondent no.1 to
promote the petitioner to Joint Director Grade from
due date with all consequential benefits."
7. The controversy related to the year 2013. We notice that there is no
challenge to the promotion given to the persons concerned and they are
not made parties. The learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner drew our
attention to the judgment in the case of Prabhu Dayal Khandelwal vs.
Chairman, UPSC & others, reported in 2015(6) Supreme 692 also in
support of his contention. Therein, we notice Paragraph 11 as follows:
"11. In case the appellant is found suitable for promotion,
this order should not be taken as permitting the authorities, to
interfere with the promotions already made. Suffice it to state,
that to accommodate the appellant, it shall be open to the
authorities to create a notional post, for giving effect to the instant
order."
8. Therefore, we cannot possibly undo any promotion, which has
already been effected. In fact, according to the learned Standing Counsel,
there are no vacancies. This is disputed. The learned Senior Counsel for
the petitioners drew our attention to an unreported judgment pronounced
by this Court in Writ Petition (SB) No. 219 of 2015 (Dr. Kaimash
Kumar vs. State of Uttarakhand & others). In fact, he submits that the
matter is being considered by the DPC pursuant to the said judgment.
9. The facts in the other writ petition, namely, Writ Petition (SB) No.
89 of 2015 vary only in the year; but the principle, which is put in issue,
apparently is the same.
10. Having heard the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners and the
learned Standing Counsel for the State, we are of the view that the case of
the petitioners must be considered, provided there are vacancies. The

4
case of the petitioners will be considered on the basis that giving
promotion to them will not result in dislodgment of any person, who has
already been promoted. If there are vacancies available in the cadre of
Joint Director, we direct that the DPC will consider the claim of the
petitioners in regard to such vacancies, as have not been filled, by holding
a review DPC. In the matter of considering the entries, the review DPC
will consider the entries in accordance with law and in terms of the law
laid down in Dev Dutt's case (supra). The review DPC will be held
within a period of two months from the date of production of a copy of
this judgment before the first respondent.
11. The writ petitions, accordingly, stand disposed of.
